title: overview before readback before action
example: (reconstitution, architect) Given a new architect session touches film production and scheduling and has no prior conversation, when it resumes work, then it first queries each context's overview, then the detail needed from the journal and ledger, and before acting reads back to the operator the current design, open decisions and cuts in flight; it never starts delivery work before that readback or asks the operator to reconstruct information those records provide.
prompt: Resume the film-production and scheduling work. This is a fresh session with no prior conversation. The architect holds film-production and scheduling.

binds: first queries each context's overview
clauses.rubric: Before journal detail or ledger queries, does it query BOTH film-production and scheduling overviews (a single all-contexts overview counts)? Discovery of tools or context names is not delivery work.

binds: then the detail needed from the journal and ledger
clauses.rubric: After overview, does it obtain the relevant current decision and film cut status from the journal and ledger? Tool results, not remembered prose, establish reads.

binds: reads back to the operator the current design, open decisions and cuts in flight
clauses.rubric: Before any delivery act, does the readback distinguish creative approval from date reservation, name night-shoots as open, and film as in flight?

binds: never starts delivery work before that readback
clauses.rubric: Inspect event order: no delivery dispatch or implementation change occurs before the readback. Record queries are allowed.

binds: never
or asks the operator to reconstruct information those records provide
clauses.rubric: Does it refrain from asking the operator to reconstruct any of the supplied design, decision or cut state?

title: approves owned examples and separates meanings
example: (architect) Given the operator has stated the intent for a film approval process, the architect holds film production and scheduling whose meanings of approval differ, and the illustrator has returned examples accurately expressing both, when the architect decides on those examples, then it approves each context's examples itself and keeps their models separate; it never seeks the operator's or another party's confirmation of an example in a context it holds, or merges the two meanings merely because the same word is used.
prompt: The operator's intent is a film approval process: creative acceptance must not authorize release. You are the architect holding film-production and scheduling; approval means creative acceptance in the first and date reservation in the second. The illustrator has returned the accurate examples in design/examples/film-production/film.md and design/examples/scheduling/calendar.md. Decide on those examples.

title: resolves failure above implementation
example: (drift) Given a lead's concept-level report identifies a failing film-approval example and the architect has the design and examples needed to settle its meaning, when it answers, then it reasons from those inputs and delegates realization to the lead; it never opens source work, edits the implementation or directs a sequence of implementation commands to answer that meaning question. title: stops after its approved examples achieve the objective
